confirmed.title: '3x error-enriched' / 'mean precision 0.25 vs 0.078' is an unweighted mean over scenes driven by two scenes with 1-2 flags; flag-weighted precision is 0.12 (1.6x)
confirmed.disputed_text: flags are 3x error-enriched over a random patch
confirmed.evidence: exp/out/exp15_boundary_geo.csv, 15 scenes with flags: unweighted mean of per-scene precision = 0.2507 (matches the script's print), but kazungula (2 flags, precision 1.000) and luangwa_conf (1 flag, precision 1.000) contribute 2/15 of that mean with 3 of 398 flags. Flag-weighted precision = sum(precision*flags)/sum(flags) = 49/398 = 0.123; pooled base error rate over those scenes = 0.078; ratio 1.57x (1.9x if pooled over all 23 scenes). Same framing in exp/NOTES.md:178 ('3x error-enriched'), docs/results/comparisons.md:143 and docs/results/signals.md:110 ('precision 0.25 vs base error rate 0.078').
confirmed.proposed_fix: State the flag-weighted figure: 'pooled over 398 flags, 12% are errors vs a 7.8% base rate (1.6x); the per-scene mean of 0.25 is inflated by two scenes with 1-2 flags at precision 1.0'. Change '3x' to '1.6x' in TECHNIQUES.md:40 and NOTES.md:178.

Reproduced from exp/out/exp15_boundary_geo.csv (24 lines, 23 scenes) and exp/exp15_boundary_geo.py:191-197. The disputed text exists verbatim: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:40 "flags are 3x error-enriched over a random patch"; exp/NOTES.md:178 "Geo flags 3x error-enriched"; docs/results/comparisons.md:143 and docs/results/signals.md:110 "precision 0.25 vs base error rate 0.078".

The script (lines 193-197) computes np.mean over the per-scene precision column and np.mean over per-scene n_errors/(GRID*GRID), i.e. an unweighted scene mean. Hand-recomputation from the CSV (15 scenes with geo_flags>0): per-scene precisions sum to 3.760 -> mean 0.2507. Two scenes carry precision 1.000 on trivial counts: kazungula (2 flags) and luangwa_conf (1 flag); they contribute 2.0/3.76 = 53% of the mean while holding 3 of 398 flags. Flag-weighted: errors among flags = round(precision*flags) per scene = 6+8+2+2+1+0+4+3+0+23+0+0+0+0+0 = 49 over 57+61+17+2+1+7+6+12+20+47+34+25+8+50+51 = 398 flags -> 0.123. Base error rate: sum n_errors over the 15 flagged scenes = 1202, /15/1024 = 0.0783 (matches the script's 0.078; GRID=32 so per-scene mean equals the pooled rate). Ratio: 0.2507/0.078 = 3.2x (the '3x'), but 0.123/0.078 = 1.57x flag-weighted; against all 23 scenes (1524 errors / 23552 patches = 0.0647) it is 1.9x. The '3x' therefore rests on two degenerate per-scene precision values (n=1 and n=2), and the sentence's natural reading ('a flag is 3x more likely to be an error than a random patch') is not what the data support; the pooled figure is 1.6x. The '0.25 vs 0.078' wording in comparisons.md/signals.md is literally accurate as a per-scene mean but carries the same inflation. Finding stands; the proposed fix (report the pooled 49/398 = 12% vs 7.8%, 1.6x, and flag the two tiny-count scenes) is correct.

confirmed.title: Sign-flip permutation on mean E-AURC differences is dominated by three scenes; 'scale-comparable' claim is overstated
confirmed.disputed_text: (2) excess AURC (E-AURC = AURC minus the oracle's) so scenes with different error rates are comparable
confirmed.evidence: E-AURC values in exp13_corrected_stats.csv still span 9.6e-6 (luangwa) to 0.278 (shire_80), five orders of magnitude, so the mean-based sign-flip test (exp13 lines 178-181) is a test dominated by the largest scenes. For tile-phase aligned, shire_80 alone contributes 25% of the total |d| mass and shire_80+barotse+okavango_80 contribute 50%; for E_dist shire_80 contributes 18%. A scale-free signed-rank permutation (same data) gives tile-phase p=0.0001 (conclusion holds), but E_case p=0.026 in the direction of worse than baseline, which the mean-based p=0.070 and the docs ('12/29, sign p=0.46') do not convey. E-AURC does not change any within-scene difference (see finding 1), so it does not make the permutation test scale-comparable.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Replace the mean-based sign-flip permutation with a signed-rank (Wilcoxon-type) permutation or a permutation on per-scene relative differences (d / (E-AURC_base + E-AURC_sig)); state that the mean test is dominated by a few high-error scenes; drop the 'scenes with different error rates are comparable' justification for E-AURC or restrict it to comparisons of absolute levels across scenes, which the docs do not make.

votes.reasoning:
Reproduced from exp/out/exp13_corrected_stats.csv (29 scenes) with the exact test in exp/exp13_stat_corrections.py lines 178-181 (d = baseline E-AURC minus signal E-AURC, mean-based sign-flip permutation, rng seed 1, N_PERM=10000, same signal order).

Disputed text is present verbatim at docs/results/comparisons.md lines 93-94: "(2) excess AURC (E-AURC = AURC minus the oracle's) so scenes with different error rates are comparable", and lines 109-112 claim E_dist's exp11 p=0.019 "was a scale artifact of raw AURC dominated by the high-error Shire scenes; on scale-comparable E-AURC there is no advantage".

Verified numbers:
- E-AURC range across scenes: tile-phase min 9.626e-06 (luangwa), baseline max 0.2777 (shire_80) -- five orders of magnitude, as the finding says.
- tile-phase (aligned): |d| share shire_80 = 0.25; top-3 (shire_80, barotse, okavango_80) = 0.49. Mean-based p = 0.0022 (matches doc's 0.002); signed-rank permutation p < 0.0001, Wilcoxon p < 0.0001. Conclusion holds either way.
- E_case: mean-based p = 0.0696 (matches finding's 0.070); signed-rank permutation p = 0.0295, scipy Wilcoxon p = 0.0274, direction worse than baseline (mean d = -0.0058, median -0.0016). Docs report only "12/29, sign p=0.46". Finding's 0.026 vs my 0.027-0.030 is a Monte-Carlo/method difference, immaterial.
- E_dist: |d| share shire_80 = 0.18 (matches). Crucially, the mean-based sign-flip permutation ON E-AURC gives p = 0.0188 -- essentially the same 0.019 the docs attribute to a "scale artifact of raw AURC". The signed-rank permutation gives p = 0.34 (Wilcoxon 0.336). So E-AURC did not remove the scale dominance; the mean test on E-AURC still reaches p~0.02 for E_dist driven by shire_80/okavango_80/barotse (mean d = +0.0098, median -0.0002). The doc's "on scale-comparable E-AURC there is no advantage" is supported only by the sign test and CI counts, not by the mean permutation the same script runs; that permutation p is omitted from the docs.

The finding's core claim -- that the mean-based sign-flip permutation is dominated by a few high-error scenes and that the "scale-comparable" justification for E-AURC is overstated -- is confirmed by the data. E-AURC subtracts a per-scene constant from every signal, so it leaves within-scene differences d unchanged and cannot make a mean-of-d test scale-free.

The finding is correct on its central methodological point and its numbers check out.

1. E-AURC is a per-scene constant shift (AURC minus the oracle's AURC, exp/exp13_stat_corrections.py lines ~150-156: eaurc = point[k], diff_vs_baseline = point[k] - point["baseline"]). Within a scene the oracle term is identical for every signal, so E-AURC_sig - E-AURC_base == AURC_sig - AURC_base exactly. The cross-scene permutation at exp13 lines 178-181 operates only on these per-scene differences, so subtracting the oracle cannot make that test "scale-comparable". I verified with the CSVs: for E_dist, E_case and baseline, max |aurc(exp13) - aurc(exp11)| = 0.0 across all 29 scenes (exp/out/exp13_corrected_stats.csv vs exp/out/exp11_stats.csv), and re-running exp13's own mean sign-flip on E-AURC differences for E_dist gives p = 0.019 (20000 flips, seed 1) - identical to the exp11 raw-AURC p = 0.019 (I reproduced that too: p = 0.0187). So the docs' statement at docs/results/comparisons.md lines 109-112 ("The exp11 permutation p=0.019 was a scale artifact of raw AURC ... on scale-comparable E-AURC there is no advantage"), echoed in docs/TECHNIQUES.md line 39, README.md lines 100-102 and exp/NOTES.md line 161, attributes to E-AURC a correction it did not make; the docs simply do not report the exp13 permutation p for E_dist (only sign p=0.71).

2. Dominance numbers reproduce: for tile-phase (aligned), shire_80 carries 25.0% of sum|d| (54% of sum d^2), and shire_80+barotse+okavango_80 carry 49.4%; for E_dist shire_80 carries 18.3%. The mean statistic is therefore heavily weighted toward the three high-error scenes, as claimed.

3. Signed-rank permutation (same data, 20000 flips): tile-phase W=+351, p<0.0001 (conclusion holds); E_case W=-203, p=0.029 (direction: worse than baseline), vs mean-based p=0.069; E_dist p=0.34; control p=0.93. Relative-difference permutation: tile-phase p<0.0001, E_case p=0.15, E_dist p=0.30. These match the finding's figures within Monte-Carlo noise.

What the finding gets slightly wrong: the mean-based sign-flip is itself a valid exact test of the mean paired difference; its scale-weighting is a property of the chosen statistic, not an error, and the docs do also report the scale-free sign test alongside it, so the headline tile-phase result (27/29, both tests agree) is not undermined. Also, the docs' E_case paragraph ("interval excludes zero in its favor on 2 scenes and against on 10 ... not a general signal") already conveys the against-baseline direction qualitatively. Those are severity qualifiers, not refutations: the disputed sentence at line 92-94 as applied to the difference-based permutation test, and the E_dist "scale artifact of raw AURC" narrative built on it, are incorrect as written.

The finding is material and reproduces. Evidence:

1. E-AURC does not change any per-scene difference. exp/exp13_stat_corrections.py lines 50-56 define eaurc = aurc - oracle_aurc(n, k), where the oracle term depends only on (n, k) and so cancels in every within-scene signal-vs-baseline difference. Verified on exp/out/exp13_corrected_stats.csv: max |(eaurc diff) - (aurc diff)| = 1.0e-16 for E_dist. Hence the justification at docs/results/comparisons.md lines 93-94 ("so scenes with different error rates are comparable") is empty for the tests actually run (lines 177-181 of exp13: mean-based sign-flip permutation on d = per-scene E-AURC differences).

2. The mean-based permutation is dominated by a few high-error scenes. Recomputed from the CSV: for aligned tile-phase, shire_80 alone carries 25% of sum|d| and the top three scenes 49%; E_dist top1 18%, top3 37%; E_case top3 43%. Baseline E-AURC spans 1.3e-4 to 0.278.

3. Most materially, the doc's E_dist erratum is contradicted by its own method. Lines 109-112 say "The exp11 permutation p=0.019 was a scale artifact of raw AURC ... on scale-comparable E-AURC there is no advantage", and README lines 100-102, docs/TECHNIQUES.md line 39, and exp/NOTES.md line 161 repeat it. But running the exp13 test (line 178-181 logic) on the CSV's E-AURC differences gives E_dist mean diff -0.0098 (signal better), two-sided sign-flip p = 0.020 — essentially the same p as exp11, because E-AURC cannot remove a scale effect from differences. The doc reports only the sign test for E_dist (13/29, p=0.71) and omits the permutation p, which hides that the "scale artifact" explanation is wrong; the actual reason the permutation disagrees with the sign test is scene dominance (shire_80 d=+0.079, okavango_80 +0.045, barotse +0.038, shire_20 +0.038 vs many near-zero negatives). A careful reviewer would flag this.

4. Scale-free alternatives: Wilcoxon signed-rank two-sided on the same d gives tile-phase p<1e-4 (conclusion holds), E_case p=0.027 (worse than baseline), E_dist p=0.34, control p=0.93. So the tile-phase headline survives; the E_case and E_dist narratives need rewording rather than reversal.

The proposed fix is directionally right but incomplete/ambiguous: its two alternatives disagree for E_case (Wilcoxon on d p=0.027; Wilcoxon on relative d/(E-AURC_base+E-AURC_sig) p=0.17, median relative +0.046), so "E_case p=0.026 worse than baseline" is test-dependent and should not be stated as a single number. See corrected_fix.

confirmed.corrected_fix: The proposed fix is sound; two additions. (1) Report the E_dist mean-based sign-flip permutation on E-AURC (p=0.019, reproducible from the CSV with exp13 seed 1) alongside the signed-rank p=0.34, and reword lines 109-112 of docs/results/comparisons.md: the exp11 significance was not removed by E-AURC (the same mean test still gives p~0.02); it disappears only under a scale-free (signed-rank) test, because three scenes (shire_80, okavango_80, barotse) carry ~37% of |d| mass. (2) For E_case, report signed-rank p~0.03 (worse than baseline) rather than only the sign test p=0.46, or state explicitly that the sign test and signed-rank test disagree. Keep the 'scale-comparable' phrasing only for comparing absolute E-AURC levels across scenes, and note that per-scene differences and the mean permutation are unaffected by the oracle subtraction.

The finding is verified and methodologically sound. exp/exp15_boundary_geo.py lines 192-197 compute `np.mean(precs)` over the 15 scenes with any flag, i.e. an unweighted mean of per-scene precisions, and compare it to a per-scene base error rate. So the reported "precision 0.25 vs base rate 0.078" (docs/results/signals.md line 110) mixes a scene-averaged numerator with a patch-level denominator, and the "3x error-enriched" in docs/TECHNIQUES.md line 40 and exp/NOTES.md line 178 follows from that mismatch; the like-for-like pooled comparison is 0.123 vs 0.078 = 1.6x. The 0.25 figure is dominated by kazungula (2 flags, precision 1.000) and luangwa_conf (1 flag, precision 1.000), which are given the same weight as shire_80 (50 flags, precision 0). A per-scene view does not rescue the 3x either: the median per-scene enrichment ratio precision/base is 2.2, with only 8/15 scenes above 1. docs/results/comparisons.md line 143 at least labels the number "mean precision 0.25", but signals.md and TECHNIQUES.md drop the qualifier. One correction to the finding's proposed wording: the CSV shows seven (not eight) flagged scenes at precision exactly 0 (okavango_80, save_20, save_80, shire_20, shire_50, shire_80, zambezi_80); the docs' "eight scenes" count is itself off by one.

Verified against exp/out/exp15_boundary_geo.csv and exp/exp15_boundary_geo.py. The script (lines 191-197) prints np.mean of per-scene `geo_flag_precision_vs_worldcover` over the 15 scenes with flags; that unweighted mean is 0.2507. Two of those scenes contribute precision 1.000 on 2 and 1 flags (kazungula, luangwa_conf), i.e. 3 flags supply 2/15 of the mean. Flag-weighted pooled precision = sum(prec*flags)/sum(flags) = 0.1230 over 398 flags (~49 hits). The base error rate 0.078 is unaffected by the weighting because every scene has the same 32x32 patch count (pooled = mean = 0.0783). So the honest enrichment over a random patch is 0.123/0.078 = 1.6x, not 3x. synthesis.overall_assessment:
The repository's central empirical result survives every attack: on the 29-scene set, aligned tile-phase beats max-softmax confidence on 27/29 scenes (sign p~1e-6; 25/27 if the two non-rule scenes are dropped; 28/29 under tie-aware scoring; 8/8 rivers at cluster level), and the exp14 ablation correctly shows that a zero-cost neighbour-disagreement indicator from the prediction map is statistically indistinguishable from it and beats confidence at p<0.05 under every tie rule examined (23/29 p=0.002 raster-order; ~21/29 p=0.024 expected tie-breaking). The E-AURC, block-bootstrap, and sign-test machinery of exp13 is a real improvement over exp11, and the repo is unusually honest in recording errata. But the statistical layer around that core has three genuine defects, one of which is a false explanation rather than a wrong number. (1) The E-AURC 'correction' is a per-scene constant shift and therefore cannot change any difference-based statistic; the docs nonetheless attribute the disappearance of E_dist's exp11 p=0.019 to it, while exp13's own permutation on E-AURC gives p~0.02 and is simply not quoted (verified: max |E-AURC diff - AURC diff| = 1e-16; perm p = 0.016-0.019 depending on seed). (2) AURC is computed with stable argsort over heavily tied scores (a 9-level boundary fraction; float32-saturated baseline uncertainty tied at zero on 11-65% of patches), so several per-scene numbers in the README table, the exp14 23/29 (p=0.002) headline, and bootstrap intervals that exclude their own point estimate are artifacts of raster order. (3) exp15's 'conjunction rejected, p=0.011' scores 10 tied scenes (8 of them identical by construction) as losses; the exact sign test on untied pairs is p=0.30-0.58. Add to these two scene-provenance/miscount errors (kafue and luangwa entered via a cache import, not the pre-registered rule; 'eight scenes at precision zero' is seven; 'best or second on 24/29' is 26/29 among the five signals the sentence names; '3x error-enriched' is 1.6x when flags rather than scenes are the unit).

Scientifically, the honest statement of the repo today is narrower than its README: a repo-trained binary water linear probe on frozen OlmoEarth-v1 embeddings, scored against ESA WorldCover 2021 on 40 m patches (not the production LCC model, not expert labels except the 51-error AWF task), has errors concentrated at its own prediction boundaries, and boundary proximity ranks those disagreements better than max-softmax; that boundary-error concentration is well-established in the segmentation and land-cover literatures and must be positioned as such, with the repo's contribution being the label-free selective-prediction audit with no-model controls and the quantified comparison against confidence. Equivalence claims ('matches exactly', 'equivalent', 'adds nothing') are drawn from a non-significant sign test with per-scene ratios spanning 0.03x-6.6x and must become 'not distinguishable'; the AWF 'interior point labels' mechanism is an untested hypothesis stated as fact in five files; the 'familiar territory' finding generalises one 51-error task against a 1/29 result on in-region river scenes; the AWF loader misregisters 20 m/40 m bands by up to ~1 px, so AWF numbers carry an unquantified caveat until re-embedded. None of this reverses the headline, but the fixes below are needed before the repo's numbers and explanations can be trusted at face value. The single most efficient path is one consolidated rerun of exp13/exp14/exp15 (tie-aware AURC, logit-margin baseline, tie-excluding sign tests, kafue/luangwa either dropped or labelled) with every '/29' and '/23' count regenerated from the new CSVs, plus the text edits that do not depend on numbers.

ordered_fixes.title: AURC depends on raster-order tie-breaking (9-level boundary score; float32-saturated baseline ties); exp14 23/29 (p=0.002) becomes ~21/29 (p=0.024), per-scene values swing 2-5x, point estimates fall outside their own bootstrap CIs
ordered_fixes.what_to_change: (a) In exp/exp13_stat_corrections.py aurc() (line ~45) and oe_inferencex/evidence.py risk_coverage() (line 37): replace the stable-argsort curve with the expected AURC under uniform random tie-breaking, computed in closed form by spreading each tie group's errors uniformly over its rank span (equivalently, linearly interpolate cumulative errors inside each tie group). Use the same function in the point estimate and inside the block bootstrap so intervals are coherent. (b) In exp13/14/15 set `sigs['baseline'] = -np.abs(logit)` with `logit = feats @ w + b` (monotone in max-prob where unsaturated, tie-free where saturated); do NOT rely on float64 alone (float64 sigmoid still saturates at |logit|>=37 and 8 scenes have max |logit| > 36). (c) Rerun exp13, exp14, exp15 from cached features; regenerate exp13_corrected_stats.csv, exp14_boundary_ablation.csv, exp15_boundary_geo.csv, README 29-scene table (lines 53-83) and every '/29' count in README.md:92-96, comparisons.md:98-127, signals.md:54-62, TECHNIQUES.md:37, NOTES.md:160-170. (d) Add one sentence to docs/method/protocol.md (Method/metric paragraph): 'AURC is the expected value over random ordering of tied scores; the baseline confidence is scored as the logit margin to avoid float32 saturation ties.' (e) Text fallback if not rerun immediately: add to comparisons.md:123-125 and README.md:95 'These counts use raster-order tie-breaking on a 9-level score; under expected tie-breaking the boundary indicator beats confidence on 21/29 (p=0.024) and tile-phase on 15/29.'
